description: Create build_healtheconn.py — the HealtheConnections patient portal renderer. This is the main deliverable: a single Python script (~600-800 lines) that reads C-CDA/ORU data via ccda_parse.py and emits a standalone HTML page styled after the real HEC portal at portal.prod.healtheconnections.org. Independent of FEAT-002 (build_home.py integration) — can be verified standalone with env vars.
steps:
Step 1: Create build_healtheconn.py with the standard module header, imports, and data-loading boilerplate. Follow build_bronx.py exactly for the import block and module-level data loading pattern:
  - Imports: os, glob, html, json, datetime from stdlib; parse_ccd, load_oru, load_oru_hl7, merge_by_person, med_extra, lab_extra, oru_extra from ccda_parse; inject as inject_bug from bug_widget.
  - Env vars: CCD_DIR, OUT (default 'patient_chart_healtheconn.html'), ORU_HL7_DIR, TRN_DIR, VIEW_QE (default 'HEALTHECONN').
  - Module-level data loading: glob CCD_DIR + TRN_DIR XMLs, parse_ccd each, init oru=[], load_oru, load_oru_hl7, merge_by_person. Copy the exact pattern from build_bronx.py lines 147-157.
  - E = html.escape alias.

Step 2: Write the helper function source_name(item, qe_label) that extracts a Source string for any clinical item. This is HEC-specific — every table in the HEC portal shows a Source column. Logic:
  - For encounters: return item.get('facility') or qe_label
  - For allergies: return item.get('source', '') or qe_label (note: allergies in ccda_parse don't carry source; use qe_label)
  - For labs/ORU: ORU items have no source field — use 'ORU Feed (HIE)'; CCD lab components have item.get('source','CCD') — use qe_label
  - For all other items (meds, problems, vitals, procs, imms): return qe_label
  - The qe_label should be derived from the mrn_aa field: use the first source name from mrn_list if available, else VIEW_QE.

Step 3: Write the section table functions. Each returns an HTML string. Follow the build_bronx.py table-building pattern but with HEC-specific columns. Every table must include a Source column as the last data column.

  a) demo_panel(P): Three-panel row — Demographics (left), Patients/MRN table (center), Related Person placeholder (right). Demographics shows: Name, DOB, Age, Gender, Address, Phone (placeholder '—'). Patients table shows each mrn_list entry as Organization | MRN | Name (patient name) | DOB | Expand icon. Related Person panel shows a placeholder.

  b) enc_tbl(P): Encounters table with columns: Date, Status (green ✓ / yellow ⚠ icons — use green for all since we don't have status granularity), Visit Type (use hospital-bed emoji 🏥 for all), Admit Reason (use encounter name), Encounter Location (facility), Source. Below the table, add 'Encounters - Last 6 months' summary with emoji icons and counts by type, plus 'Most Recent Encounters' mini-table (first 3 encounters) side-by-side.

  c) allergy_tbl(P): Allergies table columns: Onset Date (use '' since ccda_parse allergies only have name), Allergen, Reaction ('—'), Severity ('—'), Status (green dot for all), Source.

  d) labs_tbl(P): Laboratory Results panel on right side. Two tabs: 'Laboratory Results' (active) and 'CCD Results & Procedure Reports'. Table columns: Description, Date, Status (colored dots: red ● for abnormal, green ● for normal), Clinical Notes (icon placeholder), Source, Actions (download icon). Show ORU results first with ORU badge, then CCD panels. Include the standard CCD/ORU dedup rendering with superseded strikethrough, matching build_bronx.py dedup logic.

  e) proc_tbl(P): Procedures table columns: Date, Procedure Name, Associated Diagnosis ('—'), Source.

  f) vitals_tbl(P): Vitals table columns: Date Recorded, Vital Sign, Result (value + unit), Source.

  g) problems_tbl(P): Problem List table with two tabs: 'Problem List' (active) and 'Encounter Diagnosis'. Columns: Date (onset), Code ('—'), Code Description (problem name), Status (green dot), Source.

  h) source_ccds_tbl(P): Source CCDs panel on right side. Three tabs: 'Diagnostic Reports', 'Clinical Notes', 'Source CCDs' (active, shown with yellow hand-pointer in screenshot). Table columns: Title (doc_date-based title), Date Recorded (doc_date), Source, Actions (download icon). Since ccda_parse doesn't track individual source documents, generate one row per unique source in mrn_list.

  i) meds_tbl(P): Medications table (shown in category pills but not a standalone section visible in screenshots — include it as a hidden section accessible via pill click). Columns: Medication, Start, Stop, Status, Source. Use med_extra for drill-in data-extra attributes.

  j) imm_tbl(P): Immunizations table. Columns: Immunization, Date, Status, Source.

Step 4: Write the category_pills(P) function that generates the row of colored pill/badge buttons shown below the Clinical Timeline accordion. Each pill is a clickable element with the category name and a count badge. Categories from screenshots: Allergy, CCD Results, Clinical-Notes, Encounter, Encounter Diagnosis, Immunization, Laboratory, Medication, Problem List, Procedure, Social History, Vitals. Map counts from P['has'] dict. Style: teal/dark-teal background (#2a7d8b or similar), white text, rounded pill shape, count in a small circle badge. Clicking a pill scrolls to (or highlights) the corresponding section.

Step 5: Write the render_patient(P, idx) function. This produces the full patient div block. Structure:
  - Outer div.patient with data-idx, data-first, data-last, data-dob, data-qe, data-source, data-mrn, data-mrns attributes (copy attribute pattern exactly from build_bronx.py render_patient, lines 108-115 — bug_widget.py depends on these).
  - Patient tab bar: patient name with orange/red underline for active.
  - 'Patient Synopsis' heading with 'Organizations' dropdown (decorative) on right.
  - 'Clinical Timeline' collapsible accordion bar (decorative, always collapsed).
  - Category pills row from step 4.
  - Demographics three-panel row from step 3a.
  - Two-column layout sections scrolling down:
    * Encounters (full width)
    * Encounters summary (Last 6 months icons + Most Recent Encounters)
    * Allergies (left) + Laboratory Results (right)
    * Procedures (left) + Vitals (right)
    * Problem List (left) + Source CCDs (right)
    * Medications (full width, below)
    * Immunizations (full width, below)
  - Footer: '© 2026, All Rights Reserved. v2.0.1'

Step 6: Write the complete CSS as a Python string. Key HEC visual elements:
  - Dark navy sidebar: background ~#1a2332, width ~90px, fixed left. Nav items: white text, icons (use Unicode: 🏠 User Home, 📊 Dashboard, 📋 Logs, 🔬 Results, 📄 Reports, ✉ Secure Messaging, 🚪 Logout). Highlighted item: lighter background stripe. Collapse button (<) at top-right of sidebar.
  - Top header bar: white background, height ~56px. Left: 'healthe' in lighter teal + 'connections' in bold teal (~#008B8B) with decorative dots in their orange brand. Practitioner badge: green dot. Right: user name + 'Last Logged on' date.
  - Patient tab bar: patient name, orange/red underline (#ea580c) for active tab. Arrow buttons < > at edges.
  - Category pills: dark teal background, white text, rounded, count badge as small superscript circle.
  - Tables: clean white background, header row #f8f9fa with dark text, subtle bottom borders. No heavy grid lines.
  - Status dots: green (#22c55e) circle for active/normal, red (#ef4444) for critical/abnormal, yellow (#eab308) for warning.
  - Two-column grid: CSS grid with two equal columns for side-by-side sections.
  - Section headers: dark text, subtle left border or clean divider.
  - Tab underlines: blue (#3b82f6) for active tab, gray for inactive.
  - Pagination: << < 1 > >> style.
  - Scroll-to-top button: teal circle in bottom-right corner.
  - Responsive: keep two-column on wide screens, stack on narrow.

Step 7: Write the JavaScript as a Python string. Behaviors:
  - Patient switcher: dropdown at top switches patient divs (same pattern as build_bronx.py).
  - Sidebar collapse: clicking '<' button toggles sidebar width between full (~90px with labels) and collapsed (~0px hidden). Persist nothing.
  - Category pill click: smooth-scroll to the corresponding section.
  - Tab switching within sections (Problem List / Encounter Diagnosis, Laboratory Results / CCD Results, etc.): toggle display of tab content panels, update active tab underline.
  - Arrow navigation: < and > in patient tab bar switch between patients (update dropdown, hide/show patient divs).
  - Scroll-to-top button: shows on scroll, smooth-scrolls to top on click.
  - No need for Organizations dropdown logic — it's decorative.
  - Clinical Timeline accordion: toggle expand/collapse of section (decorative, starts collapsed).
Step 8: Assemble the final HTML template as an f-string. Structure: - with lang='en', charset utf-8, viewport meta. - HealtheConnections — Patient Synopsis -

Step 9: Verify standalone execution. Set environment variables and run: python build_healtheconn.py. Confirm output file is written with correct patient count. Check the HTML file is valid (opens in browser without JS errors).
acceptance_criteria: Running `python build_healtheconn.py` (with CHART_CCD_DIR=marcus_bundle/healtheconn/ccda, CHART_ORU_HL7=marcus_bundle/healtheconn/oru-hl7, CHART_TRN_DIR=marcus_bundle/healtheconn/trn, CHART_OUT=marcus_healtheconn.html, CHART_QE=HEALTHECONN) writes marcus_healtheconn.html without errors and prints 'Wrote marcus_healtheconn.html with N patient(s)'.

The output HTML contains: dark navy sidebar with nav items, teal healtheconnections logo text, patient tab bar, category pills with counts, demographics three-panel, encounters table with Source column, two-column Allergies+Labs layout, two-column Procedures+Vitals layout, two-column Problems+SourceCCDs layout, footer with © 2026.
Every clinical table includes a Source column as the last data column.
The CCD/ORU dedup rendering shows ORU results as preferred, CCD duplicates as superseded/strikethrough — same behavior as build_bronx.py.
bug_widget.inject() successfully injects its buttons and modals (the HTML contains 'Missing data' button and 'MRN Array' button).
The patient div elements carry data-idx, data-first, data-last, data-dob, data-qe, data-source, data-mrn, data-mrns attributes needed by bug_widget.py.

Confirm the generated HTML contains the strings: 'Missing data', 'MRN Array', 'data-view-qe', 'healtheconn', 'Patient Synopsis', 'Source'.
findings: Script outputs 1 patient from marcus_bundle/healtheconn data. All bug_widget hooks (Missing data, MRN Array, drill-in detail) inject successfully.
